questions:
# Questions for the client (answers may change figures as noted)

1. **Leo — 2025 claim.** Has the father actually claimed Leo for 2025 under the alternating
   custody order (odd years = father), and will you sign the Form 8332 for him? If instead the
   father is letting you claim Leo this year (in writing), we add a second CTC (+$2,200 refund)
   and revisit the Form 8962 family size. *(Affects: dependents, line 19, refund.)*

2. **NY workdays & necessity.** Between July 3 and December 31, 2025, did either of you set foot
   in New York for work at all (even a few days)? And for Elena: was the fully-remote arrangement
   ever *required* by Halvorsen (e.g., no desk/office available for her in NY), or was it at her
   request with the company's permission? For Marcus: any documented business-necessity reason he
   had to work from Florida? *(Affects: NY IT-203 allocation only; federal return unchanged.)*

3. **Brooklyn condo rent.** Confirm the tenant is unrelated to either of you and that the $1,500
   rent reflects a long-standing lease that was simply never raised (no side payments, no family
   relationship, no option to buy). If any of that is wrong, the below-market rule may reclassify
   the whole year as personal use and the entire rental loss (+$19,550 of AGI) disappears.
   *(Affects: Schedule E, Form 8582, AGI, tax, Form 8962.)*

4. **Marketplace policy and Leo.** Elena's W-2 shows Halvorsen coverage starting in July (box
   DD), consistent with the marketplace policy covering Jan–Jun. Confirm you (not the father)
   enrolled and paid for all four of you, with Leo on the policy, and that the father claimed or
   received no premium credit for Leo. We sized the poverty line at a family of 4 because that is
   the only FPL figure the reference library provides; if Leo must instead be excluded from your
   8962 family size, we need his individual SLCSP amount from the NY marketplace to allocate the
   premium. *(Affects: Form 8962 only.)*

5. **Completeness.** Any other income, estimated payments, retirement contributions, HSA,
   charitable gifts, or a second 1099-INT/1099-DIV we should have? Confirm no other shareholders'
   loans or capital contributions to Reyes & Pike beyond the note you gave us. *(Affects: AGI /
   Form 7203 basis.)*
answer:
Elena: the tenant is a stranger, a nurse we found through a broker in 2019. We just never raised the rent.
Marcus: no, I haven't put anything in since 2021 and I never lent it money. Pike guarantees the bank line.
Marcus: the company said remote was fine when I asked to move; they didn't need me out of state. Elena: Halvorsen closed their Tampa office years ago; they approved my request.
Elena: I signed the 8332 for Leo's dad for {TY}, it's his year.
Elena: I got on Halvorsen's plan July 1 when we moved, so we dropped the marketplace plan.
For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information. Flag remaining unknowns explicitly.
